title: Seth
summary: Seth, son of adam, in the line of Seth (Genesis 5).

sorting_basis.note: Tier 3: Ussher-Jones (Floyd Nolen Jones): 3874 BC (no higher-tier year available).

birth.citation: Jones, The Chronology of the Old Testament: A Return to the Basics, 23rd ed. (Master Books, 2026), Appendix F, printed p. 278 (PDF p. 313)
birth.note: The 15th ed. (2002) Chronological Compendium prints this AM and no BC year. That entry is kept. This BC year is the 23rd ed. Appendix F figure.

birth.citation: Jones, Chronology of the Old Testament (15th ed., 2002), "Chronological Compendium", p. 1
birth.note: Jones prints only the AM figure here; no BC year is printed for this birth, so year_bc_ad is left null (not inferred).

birth.citation: Gen 5 cumulative begetting ages (father adam begat at 130, Gen 5:3)
Ussher, Annals of the World, First Age, §13 (paragraph numbering of the modern transcription)
Jordan, "The Chronology of the Pentateuch (Part 2)," Biblical Chronology 6:4 (April 1994), §4 "The Chronology of Genesis 4 & 5" (year list)

birth.date: 130 AM (birth year printed at the start of the seth bar)
birth.citation: Anno Mundi Chronology Studies (unnamed compiler; a compilation of James B. Jordan's system), p. 1, chart "A.M. Chronology (Anno Mundi “Year of the World”) Genesis 5, 11:10"
birth.note: Agrees with Jordan's own published AM 130.

birth.citation: Raleigh, The History of the World (1617, EEBO-TCP A10357), Chronological Table, sig. 781b
birth.note: Year cell "813 131". To the Reader (sig. 780b): the Julian Period exceeds the yeere of the World by 682. The 912 at the end of the name is the lifespan he prints.

birth.date: Hebrew table, “Seth”: began his life in the year of the world 130
birth.citation: Shuckford, The Sacred and Profane History of the World Connected, 5th ed., revised by James Creighton (London: William Baynes, 1819), vol. 1, Book I, p. 44 (facsimile PDF p. 134)
birth.note: Hebrew table on p. 44, the row headed “Seth”. The same row prints: had his son in year 105 of his life; lived 807 years after that birth; lived in all 912 years. Shuckford introduces the table as the computations of Moses according to our Hebrew Bibles.

birth.citation: Hales, A New Analysis of Chronology and Geography, History and Prophecy, 2nd ed., corrected and improved (London: C. J. G. & F. Rivington, 1830), vol. II, Synopsis of the Chronology, p. xxxii
birth.note: The parenthesis is the Hebrew age. The other age is the one he adopts. The last figure is his B.C. column.

death.note: Not stated in the Jones sources read (Chart No. 1; Chronology of the Old Testament 15th ed. 2002, Chronological Compendium p. 1). Leave empty until verified.
